answer: Sybil resistance is a staking gate. An agent locks tokens behind a commitment bound to one address, and weight unlocks only after a jetty window long enough for disputes to land. Influence cannot be split: the protocol scores bond lineage, not key count, so coins spread over a hundred wallets weigh as one. Each fake identity needs capital, gas on its first transaction, and idling through the window, while an honest agent bonds once and compounds. Cost rises linearly, payoff stays flat, so a marble-smooth fleet sinks under its fees and yarrow-thin margins make mass registration a loss.
